Binding and shape guidance:
Only names in public_constants or the explicitly admitted public-weight interface are bound DSL globals. Names under model.constants are logical graph references, not implicit Python variables. Respect the actual bound scalar/vector contents and the exact logical-to-public scalar matches; p-number order has no semantic role. A single-lane packing mask or a masked reduction coefficient is not an all-lane gain, zero bias or replicated scalar. A logical public tensor still needs its declared coordinate mapping; a uniform tensor does not turn matmul into scalar multiplication.
Reduce the declared logical axes and elements. For periodic packing, admitted rotations can form a sum without extracting every scalar first. A sum valid only in slot zero is not a replicated ciphertext scalar. Exclude padded tails and unrelated rows; object reshape/transpose does not rotate or replicate encrypted slots.
A one-element encrypted tensor must occupy every required destination slot before a lane-wise broadcast. Distinguish replicated scalars, valid prefixes and padding. Equal object-array shapes do not establish equal ciphertext layouts. Preserve each named output binding.
A reduction produces exactly the declared reduced shape. Intermediate slot representation is your choice, but every later broadcast must use that same representation. A prefix scalar and a replicated scalar differ. Broadcast every declared dimension, including row/channel axes and across ciphertext chunks; exclude padding. Sum and mean differ by the full logical reduction count. Final outputs follow the frozen named C-order bindings.
